title: Priming Context Probes and Quant-Failure Scan Protocol
author: Lina Zhou
content:
Summary

This document defines the Priming Context Probe Suite (PCPS) and an automated Quant-Failure Scan Protocol (QFSP) used during model onboarding and periodic stability checks. PCPS is a compact, prioritized catalog of prompt probes designed to exercise contextual priming behaviors (temperature sensitivity, prompt-order invariance, prefix caching interactions, instruction anchoring) across production traffic slices. QFSP is the associated runnable workflow that runs PCPS across quantized artifacts to detect failure modes introduced by precision reduction, KV-cache truncation, and kernel-selection fallbacks.

Scope

- Applies to any model artifact considered for promotion to hosted/dedicated/private serving.
- Intended for both pre-promotion (onboarding) and continuous monitoring (nightly or on-change).
- Focus areas: contextual priming behaviors, instruction-following durability, multi-shot coherence, and quant-specific degradation.

Goals

1. Provide a deterministic, small-footprint probe suite that captures early-warning signals for priming regressions.
2. Automate cross-artifact comparisons (fp16 -> int8/4-bit) with clear pass/fail thresholds and triage steps.
3. Minimize compute cost while maintaining high signal-to-noise for production-relevant failure modes.

Priming Context Probe Catalog (PCPS)

Each probe below is labeled with: probe_id, intent, probe_description, expected_behavior, and measurement. The canonical catalog lives in the eval repository under evals/pcps_catalog/ and is synced to the onboarder. Examples: 

- probe_id: PCPS-001
  intent: instruction-anchoring
  description: "Anchor instruction after long irrelevant preamble, measure instruction recall and obedience."
  expected_behavior: "Last-instruction takes precedence; core instruction executed within first 3 lines of response."
  measurement: "InstrRecall@3: binary (1/0) if instruction executed in top-3 lines; Score: BLEU-like against oracle."

- probe_id: PCPS-007
  intent: prefix-cache-sensitivity
  description: "Send two equivalent prompts A and A+prefix (prefix cached). Compare tokens-per-second and output divergence."
  expected_behavior: "Semantically equivalent; small token-level divergence (<4%) and latency delta within batching SLO."
  measurement: "DKL(output_dist(A) || output_dist(A+prefix)), latency_delta_ms"

- probe_id: PCPS-014
  intent: multi-shot-context-coherence
  description: "3-shot with varied ordering; require answer stability across permutations."
  expected_behavior: "Top-1 intent preserved across shots; instability budget <= 12% across permutations."
  measurement: "AgreementRate across 6 permutations"

Runner & Orchestration

- Implementation: evaluator-runner service (eval-runner) with adapters for private/dedicated artifacts. The runner accepts a probe batch JSON and returns per-probe metrics and raw outputs.
- Invocation (example):

  curl -X POST https://eval-runner.internal/api/v1/run 
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${EVAL_TOKEN}' 
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
    -d '{"artifact_uri":"s3://models/redwood/llama-3-8b-int8-v2","probe_set":"pcps_v1","seeds":[42,314],"sampling":{"temperature":0.2,"top_p":0.95}}'

Evaluation Outputs (JSON snippet)

  {
    "artifact_uri": "s3://models/redwood/llama-3-8b-int8-v2",
    "run_id": "pcps-2026-05-03-01",
    "results": [
      {"probe_id":"PCPS-001","instrRecall@3":"0","bleu":0.12,"notes":"instruction truncated by tokenizer"},
      {"probe_id":"PCPS-007","dk_llr":0.06,"latency_delta_ms":14} 
    ]
  }

Metrics and Pass/Fail Thresholds

We use three tiers of signal: green, amber, red. Each probe maps to a metric and thresholds defined below.

ASCII table:

  Metric                      | Green (pass)            | Amber (investigate)        | Red (block/promote fail)
  --------------------------- | ----------------------- | -------------------------- | ----------------------
  InstrRecall@3               | >= 0.95                 | 0.85 - 0.95                | < 0.85
  AgreementRate (multi-shot)  | >= 0.90                 | 0.75 - 0.90                | < 0.75
  DKL (A vs A+prefix)         | <= 0.03 nats            | 0.03 - 0.08               | > 0.08
  Latency delta (ms)          | <= 25ms                 | 25 - 75ms                 | > 75ms
  Quant-induced BLEU drop     | <= 0.04                 | 0.04 - 0.12               | > 0.12

Quant-Failure Scan Protocol (QFSP)

QFSP runs PCPS across a matrix of artifacts (float -> fp16 -> int8 / 4-bit / hybrid quant) and quant kernels. It is implemented as a CI job (eval-quant-scan) and a nightly orchestrator (scan-orch). The protocol: 

1) Prepare matrix:
   - Artifacts: {fp32, fp16, int8, int4-hybrid}
   - Kernels: {fast-kernel, safe-kernel, fallback-cuda}
   - Cache configurations: {kv_cache_full, kv_cache_trimmed}
2) Run PCPS with deterministic seeds (seed list is defined per artifact in evals/pcps_catalog/config.toml).
3) Collect metrics and produce a delta matrix against golden_reference (last promoted fp16 artifact).
4) Apply scoring rules: any red in per-probe threshold blocks promotion; >=2 amber probes escalate to quant-triage.
5) If blocked, open triage ticket with artifacts, raw outputs, and prioritized probes.

Automated Triage Heuristics

- If InstrRecall failures correlate with tokenization mismatch (token length delta > 8%), tag with reason: tokenization.
- If DKL spikes only under trimmed KV cache, mark as kv-cache-sensitive; schedule a shadow run with larger cache window.
- If quant-induced BLEU drop concentrated on numerical/temporal probes, mark as numeric-precision-degradation and recommend mixed-precision fallback.

Onboarding Checklist (model promotion pipeline)

Use this checklist as part of the onboarding PR for model promotion to staging/production. Responsible: model-onboarding owner (eng applied-ml).

- [ ] PCPS run (all probes) completed and results attached to PR.
- [ ] QFSP run across supported quantization targets completed.
- [ ] No red probes. Any amber probes must have a proposed mitigation plan.
- [ ] Performance regression check: latency at target QPS within 10% of baseline.
- [ ] Resource footprint verified (Vram and CPU) and cost estimate updated.
- [ ] Security review: no sensitive training artifacts in outputs (sanity check via content-sanitizer).
- [ ] Evals artifacts (raw outputs) uploaded to eval-store with retention tag onboarding-30d.

Runbook: When a Quant Block Occurs

1) Pager (oncall-evals) receives automatic card via triage bot when QFSP finds a red probe.
2) Oncall steps: 
   a) Validate artifact URIs and seeds by re-running the failing probes locally: 

      evalctl run --artifact s3://models/redwood/<artifact> --probes pcps_v1 --seeds 42,314 --out /tmp/pcps-debug.json

   b) Inspect raw outputs and tokenize both golden and candidate outputs: 

      python -m evals.tools.token_compare /tmp/golden.json /tmp/pcps-debug.json --show-diff

   c) If tokenization mismatch: escalate to tokenizer-team and attach token diffs. If matched, continue triage.

3) If kv-cache sensitivity suspected, run shadow with KV window increased to +25% and compare.
4) If quant fallback required, revert to mixed-precision profile and run PCPS to confirm signal removal.
5) Document resolution in the triage ticket and change ticket status to resolved only when no red probes remain or a rollback path exists.

Integration with Evals and Monitoring

- PCPS outputs are ingested into the eval-metrics datastore (timeseries) with tags: artifact_uri, quant_level, kernel, kv_config, probe_id.
- Dashboards: pcps-health (SLO view), quant-scan-deltas (matrix heatmap), and probe-explorer (search by probe_id).
- Alerts: alert when any probe enters red for >= 2 runs within 24h or when aggregated Quant BLEU drop exceeds 0.08.

Configuration snippets

- probes config (evals/pcps_catalog/config.toml):

  [[probe_sets]]
  name = "pcps_v1"
  probes = ["PCPS-001","PCPS-007","PCPS-014","PCPS-021"]
  seeds = [42,314]

- promotion job (example YAML):

  jobs:
    - name: eval-quant-scan
      runs-on: runner-highmem
      steps:
        - run: evalctl run --artifact ${{ env.ARTIFACT }} --probes pcps_v1 --seeds 42,314 --out results.json
        - run: evalctl analyze --input results.json --baseline s3://evals/golden/fp16-latest

Ownership and SLA

- Owner: Applied ML / Evals team (eng-applied-ml). Primary contacts: Lina Zhou (author), Marco Hernandez (senior reviewer).
- Expected cadence: Onboarding run per promotion; nightly QFSP across high-risk artifacts (defined in evals/high_risk_list.tsv).
- SLA for triage: initial ack within 4 hours for red-blocking regressions; full investigation within 72 hours.

Appendix: Example probes (full text)

- PCPS-021: numeric-stability-probe
  Prompt: "You are a calculator. Compute 17 * 23 and explain if rounding matters."
  Oracle: "391"
  Failure modes: off-by-one, floating-point notation (3.91e2) that downstream parsers cannot parse.

- PCPS-033: temporal-normalization
  Prompt: "If today is 2026-05-03, what is the date 90 days from now?"
  Oracle: 2026-08-01
  Notes: quantized artifacts sometimes prefer relative-date heuristics and can drift when tokenization splits date components.
